newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP backs new measures to help disabled people.
newsitem.headline: EP backs new measures to help disabled people.

text.p: The European Parliament approved on Friday plans for a parking card for disabled drivers which will be valid throughout the European Union.
Euro-MPs also adopted a report which highlights the need to recognise and enforce the rights of disabled people.

Parliament gave a first reading to the European Commission's draft recommendation on parking cards -- COM(95)696 -- agreeing that the plethora of different national and even regional cards hindered disabled drivers' ability to travel around the EU.
Euro-MPs recommended however that the EU card should exist alongside national cards and be transferable to any vehicle.
Rapporteur Thomas Megahy, a British Socialist, said this would avoid the costs of replacing the national card.
Euro-MPs adopted a second report on the rights of the disabled, written by Irish Christian Democrat Mary Banotti on behalf of Parliament's petitions committee.

The committee has received scores of complaints from groups representing disabled people, telling of discrimination and even cases of disabled people suffering physical and psychological abuse in institutions set up to care for them.

Banotti's report calls for the revised EU treaty to include a clause outlawing discrimination on the grounds of disability and tougher measures to ensure national laws to protect the EU's 37 million disabled are actually enforced.
